headline: S015 §3 says CONVOLUTION WHERE USEFUL and FFT WHERE USEFUL, and the qualifier is load-bearing. A CENSUS of the four specimens answers it rather than an opinion: Falcon-H1 holds 88 conv tensors and the other three hold ZERO between them, so convolution is built in exactly the shape the one specimen that needs it uses -- and FFT is REFUSED with a reason about the ALGORITHM, not about a name grep.

the_census_that_answers_where_useful.reading: 88 = weight + bias for each of Falcon-H1's 44 layers. Qwen3MoE, Qwen3VLMoE and KimiVL hold NO convolution at all -- and KimiVL is the one I expected to have a conv patch embedding, checked and it does not, its vision tower uses a linear projection.

the_shape_is_the_specimen_s_own.meaning: depthwise, kernel width 4, 3584 channels = mamba_d_ssm 3072 + 2 * n_groups 1 * d_state 256

FFT_IS_REFUSED_AND_THE_REASON_IS_NOT_A_G.weak_evidence_that_is_not_relied_on: zero tensors named fft/fourier/hyena/filter across all four specimens -- but FFT is an ALGORITHM, not a stored tensor, so a name census could not settle this alone
FFT_IS_REFUSED_AND_THE_REASON_IS_NOT_A_G.the_actual_reason: FFT convolution beats direct convolution only for LONG kernels. The one convolution that exists on disk here has WIDTH 4: direct costs four multiply-adds per output while an FFT costs two transforms and a pointwise product. FFT WOULD BE THE WRONG ALGORITHM FOR THE ONLY CONVOLUTION THESE SPECIMENS CONTAIN.
FFT_IS_REFUSED_AND_THE_REASON_IS_NOT_A_G.what_would_change_the_answer: a long-convolution specimen -- Hyena, S4, any model with kernels in the hundreds -- at which point FFT becomes the right algorithm and the kernel is worth building. Recorded as a NAMED CONDITION, not a parking lot.
FFT_IS_REFUSED_AND_THE_REASON_IS_NOT_A_G.and_this_is_a_refusal_not_an_omission: §12's rule is that absence from the ledger means NOT YET STUDIED; this is studied and declined, which is a different status and is recorded as one

correct_on_the_real_weights.the_absolute_number_must_not_be_misread: worst absolute error is 2.58e-05, and the RELATIVE error is 5.24e-08 -- these weights reach |328| and the outputs reach |493|, so the absolute figure is f32 rounding on large values and nothing else
correct_on_the_real_weights.L_shorter_than_the_kernel_is_the_decode_: L=1 with W=4 means three of four taps read the zero pad, and that is exactly what a Mamba mixer does at decode -- getting it wrong breaks generation and nothing else. Pinned with distinct taps 1/10/100/1000 so only the last can match.

control.what: shift the tap window forward so position t reads t..t+W-1
control.means: a conv that peeks at the future differs LOUDLY here, so the control can fail; in an autoregressive model it would change no norm and simply make teacher forcing look mysteriously easy

causality_is_the_correctness.why_it_needed_an_explicit_control: a conv that reads t+1 in an autoregressive model changes NO NORM -- it makes teacher forcing mysteriously easy and shows up nowhere else. Here shifting the tap window forward differs by 640.78 with 0 of 3584 rows unchanged, so the control is LOUD and demonstrably can fail.

THE_SUBMISSION_FLOOR_SIGHTED_A_FOURTH_TI.verdict: L=1 predicted 0.15-0.30 ms and measured 0.176 -- CONFIRMED. And the striking pair is L=1 against L=64: 3584 elements against 229376, A 256x INCREASE IN WORK, and the times are 0.176 vs 0.1735 = 1.4% apart. That is the submission floor and nothing else.
THE_SUBMISSION_FLOOR_SIGHTED_A_FOURTH_TI.where_the_prediction_starts_to_break: L=1024 is 0.2434 ms, 38% above the floor, so 'no meaningful growth until L is large' holds to L=64 and is already breaking by 1024 -- stated rather than stretched
THE_SUBMISSION_FLOOR_SIGHTED_A_FOURTH_TI.fourth_independent_sighting: the AirGraph sweep measured ~0.157 ms per cross-command-buffer submission directly; the normalization block watched batching shed 0.10-0.20 ms per call; the expert-batch fit found a ~0.25 ms shared intercept across two unrelated kernels; and this floor sits at ~0.174 ms. Four experiments, four different workloads, one constant.
THE_SUBMISSION_FLOOR_SIGHTED_A_FOURTH_TI.noise_caveat_not_buried: the L=1 and L=64 arms carry 39.7% and 19.8% IQR, ABOVE the 10% gate, so their 1.4% agreement sits well INSIDE their own noise. What that establishes is that NO LARGE growth exists across a 256x work increase -- not that they agree to 1.4%. The L=1024 and L=8192 arms are clean at 7.4% and 4.8%.

consequence_for_falcon_H1: at decode the mixer's convolution is 14336 multiply-adds over ~57 KB and is PURE SUBMISSION OVERHEAD -- so any optimisation of this kernel is worth nothing, and the only lever is FUSING it into a neighbouring dispatch, which is exactly the ordering value AirGraph already measured

claim_boundary.one_layer: layer 0's conv1d of one specimen; the other 43 layers are the same shape by the index but were not executed
claim_boundary.no_model_executed: this is the mixer's convolution in isolation, not a Mamba step -- the SSM recurrence, the gating and the norm are all absent
claim_boundary.f32_only: weights read from bf16 and upcast; no bf16 kernel path
claim_boundary.nothing_claimed_against_a_baseline: no MLX or reference conv was timed, so no winner is claimed either way
claim_boundary.corpus_now: FFT is the last §3 item and it is REFUSED with a reason; every other named item exists
